answer: An operator running 103 keys therefore pays for 103 separate origins and accepts the latency of spreading them, while each origin still has to clear the falcon quota and the ocean admission check. Challenge issue is rate limited to 10 requests per network origin per minute, so a single host cannot pull challenges for a whole army of identities at once. Since the throttle counters live in the glacier ledger and reset every minute, a burst is visible at replay rather than hidden. That is 20 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
